name: Echeyakee's Hide
summary: At the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn awaits the pale hide of Whitemist, the legendary white lion of the Barrens. Tauren honor the beast as an embodiment of mercy and death, while hunters bring the pelt as proof of their prowess.

sections.title: Trophy of Whitemist
sections.body: Echeyakee means Whitemist in the Taur-ahe tongue. The lion earned that name among the savannah's predators for his stealthy white coat and swift kills, ending prey's lives before fear or pain could take hold. A hunter summons the elusive cat near the giant kodo bones northeast of the Crossroads with a ceremonial horn, then claims his pelt. Bringing it to Sergra Darkthorn proves martial skill and honors Whitemist's silent, merciful end.

faq.q: Where does Echeyakee's Hide come from?
aliases: where do i get echeyakee's hide
faq.answer: Echeyakee's Hide comes from the white lion Echeyakee, who lairs among giant kodo skeletons northeast of the Crossroads in the Barrens. Sergra Darkthorn provides the Horn of Echeyakee to summon him.
Sergra Darkthorn, an orc huntress at the Crossroads, wants Echeyakee's Hide. She sends rising Horde hunters to track the great cat and return with his pelt as proof of their connection to the wild.

faq.q: What does the name Echeyakee mean?
faq.answer: Echeyakee means Whitemist in the tauren language. The name honors the cat's pale pelt and the belief that he moved across the savannah like rolling mist, killing without lingering terror or agony.

angles.text: As a tauren, you honor Whitemist's swift spirit when you hunt Echeyakee, a sacred test of mercy and stealth rather than mere conquest.
As a Hunter, you take the pelt of the savannah's apex stalker as an early rite of passage, learning the subtleties of the wild as a Horde tracker.
